sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Holly is a symbolic plant. Common holly belongs to the genus Ilex. It is a small tree or shrub with red berries and shiny evergreen leaves. The plant stood out in snowy woodlands. People linked it to Christmas, the Christian midwinter feast. The English name comes from Middle English and relates to the word holy. Before Christianization the Celts held the tree sacred. It served as the emblem of the Holly King, the ruler of winter. The Holly King fought the Oak King. The Welsh myth of the combat between Hafgan and Arawn may preserve this seasonal fight. People pair holly with ivy. Holly stands for the masculine force. Ivy stands for the feminine. The holiday song The Holly and the Ivy keeps the link familiar.
objective: Document holly as a symbolic plant in Celtic and Christian tradition.
